synopsis: Lord Rooker's full title is The Rt Hon. the Lord Rooker. His name is Jeffrey William Rooker, and he is a current member of the House of Lords.

history.heading: Osteoporosis: Preventive Medicine
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government whether and how Osteoporosis is considered within wider preventative health policies.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Royal Osteoporosis Society
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government on how many occasions since July 2024 ministers have met representatives of the Royal Osteoporosis Society.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: National Security
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government what consideration they have given to a public information campaign on systemic state-sponsored non-military efforts that disrupt economic and political systems in the UK; and what assessment they have made of the impact of
history.answeringBodyName: Cabinet Office

history.heading: Fractures: Health Services
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government, further to the answer by Baroness Merron on 6 July (HL Deb col 2), how many Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) do not have a fracture liaison service in each of the NHS hospitals within the ICB.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Food: Hygiene
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government what are the financial or legislative barriers to making the display of food hygiene ratings mandatory in England.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Fuels: Excise Duties
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government how they intend to replace revenue from fuel duties in the light of the increasing adoption of electric vehicles.
history.answeringBodyName: Treasury

history.heading: Greenhouse Gas Emissions
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government why they do not publish data on greenhouse gas emissions embedded within the supply chain of (1) energy intensive goods, (2) car batteries, and (3) solar panels, imported into the UK.
history.answeringBodyName: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

history.heading: Clean Power: Electricity
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government whether it remains the policy of the National Energy System Operator to achieve clean electricity by 2030 and, if so, what is the effect on the UK's energy security.
history.answeringBodyName: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

history.heading: Electricity and Natural Gas: Prices
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government when they expect to break the link between electricity bills and volatile international gas prices.
history.answeringBodyName: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

history.heading: Power Failures
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government whether there is co-ordinated planning taking place within Government in respect of addressing potential power cuts in 2026 and 2027.
history.answeringBodyName: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

history.heading: Wind Power
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government whether the UK's total offshore wind capacity over the past two years has been equal to, or greater than, the total offshore wind capacity in the preceding six years.
history.answeringBodyName: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

history.heading: Clean Power: Job Creation
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government whether new jobs created over the past two years by the clean power investment programme have equalled the jobs lost in the fossil fuel industry over the same period of time.
history.answeringBodyName: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

history.heading: Leasehold: Reform
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government what assessment they have made of whether the capping of ground rents will affect the price of the purchase of the freehold by leaseholders.
history.answeringBodyName: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

history.heading: Fractures: Health Services
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government how many fracture liaison services have been established since July 2024.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Fractures: Death
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government what assessment they have made of the number of deaths each year following fractures.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Osteoporosis: Diagnosis
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government what steps they have taken since July 2024 to establish early diagnosis clinics for osteoporosis in England; and how many such clinics have been established.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Osteoporosis: Medical Treatments
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government what steps they plan to take to ensure standards of treatment for osteoporosis are consistent across England.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Sexual and Reproductive Health: Women
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government what assessment they have made of the inequalities affecting women identified in the report by Warwick University and Cysters, Women’s reproductive health in the West Midlands, published in March.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Medicine: Research
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government what steps they take when funding medical research to ensure that diseases common to males and females are studied on a separate gender basis rather than a male-only basis.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Health: Women
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government what assessment they have made of whether a health gap for females is caused by bias in medical research.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Health and Life Expectancy: Women
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government what assessment they have made, if any, of the reasons that females have a longer average lifespan, and shorter average health span, than males.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Diagnosis: Gender
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government whether they have made an assessment of diagnostics delays in health issues based on gender; and if so, what reasons they found for those delays.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Animal Experiments: Rodents
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government whether they monitor the gender of mice used in research studies that are funded by UK Research and Innovation.
history.answeringBodyName: Home Office

history.heading: Agriculture: Databases
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government what the level of public investment was in Agrimetrics from 2015 until it ceased operations.
history.answeringBodyName: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology

history.heading: Agriculture: Databases
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government how they plan to make publicly funded data accumulated by Agrimetrics available; and whether access to that data will be cost-free.
history.answeringBodyName: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology

history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government how much was (1) paid in damages to patients for clinical negligence, and (2) paid in respect claimants legal fees for latest year.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government why clinical negligence claims against the NHS are settled on the basis of costs of care in the private sector rather than those of the NHS.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Travel Information: Torture
history.questionText: To ask His Majesty's Government what assessment they have made of the merits of informing British nationals of the risk of torture in Foreign Office travel advice for countries where there is a known risk of torture.
history.answeringBodyName: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office
